text.en: Raju's uncle grew vegetables in a green house and raised fish in a pond. "That is economic biology," he said.

Horticulture is the science of growing fruits, vegetables and flowers. Pomology is fruit farming, olericulture is growing vegetables, floriculture is cultivating flowering plants and landscape gardening makes gardens beautiful. Vegetable forcing grows vegetables in buildings, green houses or other artificial conditions.
Animal manure, compost and green manure can contribute organic matter to soil. Biofertilisers contain living organisms that can help make some nutrients available to plants. Medicinal plants produce many compounds, including secondary metabolites. Some plant compounds have become sources of medicines after scientific study. Mushroom cultivation, hydroponics (growing plants in water), aeroponics and aquaponics are modern methods.
Dairy farming raises animals for milk. Aquaculture raises aquatic organisms, including fish and prawns. Vermiculture means raising earthworms, while vermicomposting uses worms to help break down organic material.

Economic biology looks at how people use knowledge of living things. Growing food, caring for livestock and producing useful materials all involve decisions about living systems.
Horticulture focuses on crops such as fruits, vegetables and flowers, as well as ornamental plants. Its courses divide these crops into areas according to what is grown.

board.text: Horticulture includes food and ornamental plants

text.en: Pomology concerns fruits such as mangoes or guavas. Olericulture concerns vegetables such as brinjal or beans. A market’s produce can illustrate the difference.
Floriculture concerns flowers and ornamental plants. Landscape gardening also considers how planted areas are placed and used, such as shade along a path.
A kitchen garden mainly supplies a household. A larger commercial vegetable garden may supply a market. The same plant could be grown in either setting.
A greenhouse or covered structure can change the conditions around a crop. The textbook calls planned out-of-season vegetable production vegetable forcing.
Compost contributes decomposed organic matter. Organic matter can help soil hold moisture and affect its structure. Soil characteristics and crop needs shape how farmers use amendments.
Green manure comes from plant material grown to add organic matter to soil. It differs from animal manure by its source.

board.text: Green manure: plant material · animal manure: livestock waste

text.en: A biofertiliser can help nutrients become available through relationships between organisms and plants. The label refers to an agricultural role and does not describe all soil amendments.

board.text: Biological activity can affect nutrient availability

text.en: Some fungi associated with roots can help a plant obtain nutrients. In return, the fungus can receive sugars from the plant. This is one example of an exchange in soil.

A plant may make compounds for defence or communication. Some such secondary metabolites have been studied by chemists for possible uses. A plant source is only the starting point for evaluating a compound.

board.text: Study the properties of the compound

text.en: Edible mushrooms are the visible fruiting structures of certain fungi. A farm can market edible species selected for food. Unfamiliar mushrooms cannot be identified as edible from appearance alone.

board.text: Mushrooms are fungi, and species differ

text.en: Hydroponics grows plants without soil by supplying water and dissolved nutrients to roots. A support can hold the plants while the roots meet the solution.
In aeroponics, roots hang in air and meet droplets of nutrient solution. Compare what surrounds the roots rather than simply asking whether water is present.
Aquaponics links aquatic animal rearing with plant production in a circulating system. In a diagram, trace water from the animal part through the plant part.

board.text: Aquaponics links aquatic animals and plant roots

text.en: Aquaculture covers the production of aquatic organisms, including some plants and animals. Pisciculture refers specifically to raising fish.

board.text: Pisciculture is one part of aquaculture

text.en: A freshwater fish example and a prawn example are both aquatic production. Identify the organism and the habitat before comparing how production is organised.
Dairy farming cares for animals that produce milk, such as cows and buffaloes. It involves animal care, feed and clean handling rather than simply the act of collecting milk.

board.text: Dairy farming includes care and milk production

text.en: Milk moving from farm to collection and processing illustrates several kinds of work. The farm supplies a product, while transport and processing connect it to people who buy it.
Vermiculture means rearing earthworms. A system using earthworms to help break down organic material is vermicomposting. One names the rearing activity and the other names a use.
Compost and vermicompost can both contribute organic material to soils. Their usefulness depends on what went into them and how the finished material is used.

board.text: Compare the source and purpose of soil amendments

text.en: When comparing production systems, identify what each one produces and what resources it uses. Concerns such as water use, waste and animal care belong in the comparison.
Sort three examples: a mango orchard, a fish pond and a covered soil-free vegetable garden. Use crop, organism and method to select the most precise term for each.

board.text: Orchard: fruit · fish pond: pisciculture · soil-free liquid: hydroponics

problem.en: Classify a mango orchard, a farm raising fish and a garden where vegetables grow with their roots supplied by a nutrient solution.

text.en: Identify fruit and fish as the two products.

why.en: Fruit growing is pomology and rearing fish is pisciculture.

text.en: Classify the vegetable garden by its growing method.

why.en: Growing plants without soil using a nutrient solution is hydroponics.

prompt.en: A friend says Hydroponics needs soil. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: Hydroponics grows plants in water with nutrients.

points.en: Horticulture grows fruit, vegetables and flowers.
